recipes.name: Käsespätzle
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft egg noodles in strings of melted mountain cheese, with sweet, deeply browned onions on top.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich dish that brings protein and calcium from the eggs and cheese; it is a hearty meal best eaten with a green salad beside it.

components.note: the whole batch of batter, scraped or pressed into boiling water

ingredients.prepNote: for the onions and the dish
in place of Allgäuer Bergkäse (mountain cheese), which the database does not hold

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (205°C) and butter a deep baking dish.
Melt most of the butter in a wide pan and fry the onion rings over medium heat, stirring often, until deep golden, 15 to 20 minutes.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the salt and press or scrape the Spätzle batter into it in batches. Lift each batch out with a slotted spoon 1 to 2 minutes after it floats.
Layer the hot Spätzle in the dish with the two cheeses, finishing with cheese.
Bake until the cheese is melted and bubbling, 15 to 20 minutes, then pile the onions on top and serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the Emmental and mountain cheese.
From the eggs in the batter and the cheese.

recipes.curationNote: Quick German Recipes, Oma's Käsespätzle for every amount and step; 4 to 6 servings: 42 g butter, 2 large onions, 360 g cooked Spätzle, 226 to 339 g Emmental; noodles cooked in salted water; no pepper or herbs, garnished with onions only.

recipes.name: Spätzle
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender, slightly chewy egg noodles with a buttery finish, made for soaking up gravy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein from the eggs and starch for energy, a plain side for a braise or a roast.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with the salt.
Press the batter through a Spätzle press or scrape it in thin strips off a wet board straight into the water, one batch at a time.
When the noodles float, give them 1 to 2 minutes more, then lift them into a colander with a slotted spoon.
Toss the drained Spätzle in the butter in a warm pan for 2 to 3 minutes and serve beside a braise or with gravy.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs in the batter.

recipes.curationNote: Both sources boil the batter in salted water until it floats and finish it in butter; the batter itself is the Spätzleteig base.

recipes.name: Maultaschen in der Brühe
recipes.flavorProfile: Large pasta pockets filled with meat, spinach and herbs, served in a clear, savoury beef broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein and iron from the beef and pork and folate from the spinach, in a warming broth.

components.note: one stale roll, soaked in milk

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.cutPrep: two for the filling, one beaten for sealing

instructions: Tear the roll into small pieces, cover with the warm milk for 5 to 10 minutes, then squeeze it out and crumble it.
Soften the onion in the butter over medium heat, about 5 minutes.
Mix the beef, pork, spinach, parsley, two eggs, salt, pepper, nutmeg, bread and onion into an even filling.

Roll the noodle dough thin into long strips about 12 cm (5 in) wide. Spread or spoon the filling along one half, brush the edges with beaten egg, fold over and press firmly, then cut into squares about 8 cm (3 in) long.
Simmer the Maultaschen in barely bubbling salted water until they float and the filling is cooked through, 10 to 15 minutes.
Lift them into bowls of hot beef broth to serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, pork and eggs.

recipes.curationNote: Quick German Recipes, Maultaschen for every amount and step; makes 6 to 8, ours 6.

recipes.name: Kartoffelknödel (Potato Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, smooth potato dumplings with a crisp buttered crouton hidden in the middle, made to sit in gravy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings potassium and vitamin C from the potatoes, with starch for energy beside a roast.

components.note: one day-old roll, cut into small cubes

ingredients.cutPrep: floury, boiled in their skins, peeled and riced
ingredients.prepNote: riced while warm and chilled for several hours
plus more if the dough is soft

instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, 20 to 30 minutes. Peel, press through a ricer while warm and chill until cold, several hours or overnight.
Fry the bread cubes in the butter over medium heat until golden on all sides, 4 to 6 minutes, and let them cool.
Work the potato starch, eggs, salt and nutmeg into the riced potatoes to a smooth dough that holds its shape.
With wet hands, shape 8 dumplings, pressing two or three croutons into the centre of each.
Lower them into a large pot of salted water kept just below a simmer and let them cook until they float and are firm, 18 to 20 minutes. Do not let the water boil hard or they break.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potatoes, cooked in their skins.

recipes.curationNote: Both sources bind riced cooked potatoes with starch and egg; Quick German Recipes adds the buttered crouton centre, kept here. Cooked just below a simmer as both say.

recipes.name: Semmelknödel (Bread Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, savoury dumplings of soaked rolls with onion, bacon and parsley, soft enough to cut with a fork.
recipes.healthBenefit: Turns stale rolls into a filling side, with protein from the eggs and milk; the bacon makes it a salty one.

components.note: five stale rolls, about 450 g, cut into 1 cm cubes
30 g, only if the mixture is too wet

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tsp, for the dough; the source says to taste

instructions: Toss the bread cubes with the salt, pour the hot milk over and leave to soak for 15 to 20 minutes.
Fry the bacon and onion in the butter until the onion is translucent, 5 to 7 minutes, then stir in the parsley.
Add the onion mixture, eggs and pepper to the bread and knead lightly with wet hands until it holds together, adding breadcrumbs only if it is too wet.
Shape 12 firm dumplings and lower them into a large pot of simmering water with 1 tbsp salt.
Cook uncovered, without boiling, until firm and cooked through, 15 to 20 minutes, then lift out with a slotted spoon.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs, milk and bacon.

recipes.curationNote: Quick German Recipes, Oma's Semmelknödel for every amount and step; serves 6, same as ours: about 450 g bread, 360 ml milk, 28 g butter, 2 eggs, bacon; onion size from My Dinner.

recipes.name: Kartoffelpuffer (Reibekuchen)
recipes.flavorProfile: Lacy, crisp-edged grated potato pancakes, soft inside, eaten hot with cool, sweet apple sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings potassium and vitamin C from the potatoes; fried in plenty of oil, they are a treat rather than an everyday dish.

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and finely grated, squeezed dry

instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion, wrap them in a towel and squeeze the liquid into a bowl. Let the liquid stand for a few minutes, pour it off and keep the starch at the bottom.
Mix the potatoes and onion with the starch, eggs, flour, salt and nutmeg.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat. Drop in heaped spoonfuls and press them flat.
Fry until deep golden and crisp, 3 to 4 minutes a side, adding oil as needed, and drain on paper.
Keep warm in a 200°F (95°C) oven while frying the rest and serve with apple sauce.
recipes.curationNote: Quantities follow My Dinner, including saving the potato starch; both sources fry in oil or clarified butter and serve with apple sauce.

recipes.name: Bratkartoffeln
recipes.flavorProfile: Slices of cooked potato fried until crisp and brown, with soft onion and salty bits of bacon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings potassium and vitamin C from the potatoes; the bacon and frying fat make it a rich side.

ingredients.cutPrep: waxy, boiled in their skins the day before, peeled and sliced 5 mm (0.25 in) thick

instructions: Fry the bacon in a large heavy pan until golden, then lift it out and leave the fat behind.
Add the clarified butter, then the potato slices in one layer, and fry over medium-high heat without stirring for about 5 minutes, until browned underneath.
Turn them, add the onion and keep frying and turning gently until crisp on both sides and the onion is soft, 8 to 12 minutes.
Return the bacon, season with salt and pepper and serve straight away.
recipes.curationNote: Quick German Recipes uses cooked potatoes, bacon and onion in butter and bacon fat; Wikipedia gives the cooked-the-day-before potato as the classic, and clarified butter is the usual German frying fat.

recipes.name: Schwäbischer Kartoffelsalat
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, warm potato slices soaked in a tangy broth and vinegar dressing with mild onion and chives, no mayonnaise.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light potato salad with potassium and vitamin C, dressed with rapeseed oil rather than mayonnaise.

ingredients.cutPrep: waxy, boiled in their skins, peeled warm and thinly sliced

instructions: Boil the potatoes whole in their skins in salted water until just tender, 25 to 30 minutes.
Meanwhile warm the broth, vinegar, mustard, salt, sugar, pepper and onion in a small pan until the sugar dissolves, without boiling.
Peel the potatoes while still warm and slice them thinly into a bowl.
Pour the warm dressing over, fold gently and leave to soak for 30 to 60 minutes, folding now and then until the salad looks creamy.
Fold in the oil and chives, taste for salt and vinegar and serve at room temperature.

citations.source: My Dinner, Authentic Swabian Potato Salad
Quick German Recipes, Southern German Potato Salad

recipes.curationNote: Follows My Dinner (beef broth, vinegar, mustard, oil, onion warmed in the dressing). Quick German Recipes confirms the warm broth method for the south.

recipes.name: Norddeutscher Kartoffelsalat
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy potato salad with mayonnaise and yogurt, crunchy pickles, egg and fresh dill.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings potassium from the potatoes and protein from the eggs; the mayonnaise makes it a rich salad.

ingredients.cutPrep: waxy, boiled, peeled and cut into bite-size pieces

ingredients.prepNote: the source says to taste; a pinch

instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft, about 20 minutes, and hard boil the eggs for 8 to 10 minutes.
Soften the onion over low heat for about 10 minutes, then stir in the warm broth, mustard, vinegar and sugar.
Peel and cut the potatoes while warm, pour the broth mixture over them and leave to cool, 20 to 30 minutes.
Fold in the mayonnaise, yogurt, pickles, eggs and dill, season with the salt and a pinch of pepper and chill for at least 1 hour before serving.

citations.source: My Dinner, Northern German Potato Salad
Quick German Recipes, Oma's Potato Salad

recipes.curationNote: My Dinner, Northern German Potato Salad for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours.

recipes.name: Schupfnudeln
recipes.flavorProfile: Finger-shaped potato noodles, soft inside and browned in butter, often tossed with sauerkraut.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings potassium from the potatoes and starch for energy; with sauerkraut beside it the plate gains fibre.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tsp in the potato water and 1 tsp in the noodle water, poured away

instructions: Boil the potatoes in water with 1 tsp salt until soft, 15 to 20 minutes, drain and let them steam dry, then peel and rice them.
Knead the warm potato with the flour, cornstarch, egg, salt and nutmeg to a smooth dough that is not sticky.
Roll walnut-size pieces between your palms into fingers about 6 cm (2.5 in) long with pointed ends.
Cook them in barely simmering water with 1 tsp salt until they float, 2 to 3 minutes, and drain.
Brown them in the butter over medium heat, 5 to 7 minutes, and scatter with parsley. Serve alone or tossed with sauerkraut.
recipes.curationNote: My Dinner, Easy Schupfnudeln for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours.

recipes.name: Salzkartoffeln
recipes.flavorProfile: Plain peeled potatoes boiled in salted water until tender and floury at the edges, the everyday German side.
recipes.healthBenefit: A simple side with potassium, vitamin C and vitamin B6 and nothing added but salt.

ingredients.prepNote: about 1 tsp per litre, poured away

instructions: Peel the potatoes, dropping them into cold water as you go so they stay white.
Quarter them, cover with fresh water in a pot and add the salt.
Bring to a boil, cover and boil gently until a knife slides in easily, about 20 minutes.
Drain, return the pot to the low heat for a minute to steam them dry and serve.
recipes.curationNote: Quick German Recipes, Oma's Salzkartoffeln for every amount and step; one potato a person, about 1 tsp salt per quart of water.

recipes.name: Kartoffelpüree
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, fluffy mashed potatoes with warm milk, butter and a breath of nutmeg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings potassium and vitamin C from the potatoes and calcium from the milk.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: 1/2 tsp, plus more for the water

instructions: Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water until very tender, 20 to 25 minutes, then drain and steam dry over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Press them through a ricer or mash them by hand, never in a blender, which turns them gluey.
Heat the milk and cream together and beat them in a little at a time with a wooden spoon, then the butter, until smooth and fluffy.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg and serve hot.
recipes.curationNote: Lecker, Klassischer Kartoffelbrei for every amount and step; 1 kg potatoes, 100 ml milk, 5 tbsp cream, 50 g butter, 1/2 tsp salt in the milk, a pinch of pepper, freshly grated nutmeg.

recipes.name: Himmel und Erde
recipes.flavorProfile: Mashed potato and apple, sweet and savoury at once, under crisp fried onions; heaven is the apple, earth the potato.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings potassium from the potatoes and fibre and vitamin C from the apples and potatoes together.

ingredients.cutPrep: floury, peeled and cut in 2.5 cm (1 in) cubes
tart cooking apples, peeled, cored and thickly sliced

instructions: Boil the potatoes and apples together in salted water until tender, 10 to 15 minutes, and drain.
Meanwhile fry the onions in half the butter over medium heat until crisp and brown, 10 to 12 minutes.
Mash the potatoes and apples with the rest of the butter and season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Spoon the onions over the mash and serve with fried blood sausage or another sausage.

citations.source: Quick German Recipes, Oma's Himmel und Erde

recipes.curationNote: Follows Quick German Recipes; Wikipedia gives the name and the usual blood sausage (Flönz) served with it, mentioned in the last step rather than listed.

recipes.name: Pellkartoffeln mit Quark
recipes.region: Across Germany, especially the north and east
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot potatoes boiled in their jackets with a cool, tangy herb quark full of chives and a little garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light meal with protein and calcium from the quark and potassium from the potatoes cooked in their skins.

ingredients.prepNote: for the cooking water; the sources say a little
the source says to taste; a usual amount for the quark
the source says to taste; a pinch
linseed oil, drizzled over, as in Lusatia

instructions: Cover the potatoes with water, add 1 tsp salt and the caraway, and boil until tender, 20 to 25 minutes.
Meanwhile stir the quark and sour cream together until smooth, then fold in the chives and garlic and season with the salt and a pinch of pepper.
Drain the potatoes and serve them hot in their skins, to be peeled at the table, with the chive quark and a drizzle of linseed oil.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the quark and sour cream.

recipes.curationNote: My Dinner, German Quark Dip for every amount and step; sour cream variation: quark, sour cream, 30 g chives, garlic, salt and pepper to taste; linseed oil 2 tbsp as in Lecker's Pellkartoffeln mit Quark.

recipes.name: Kaiserbrötchen (Kaiser Rolls)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crackling-crusted white rolls with a soft, airy crumb and the five-part star pattern on top.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain bread roll that brings carbohydrate for energy and a little protein from the wheat.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the lukewarm water and leave for 10 minutes until it foams.
Add the flour, salt and butter and knead for 8 to 10 minutes to a smooth, slightly tacky dough. Cover and let it rise until doubled, about 1 hour.

Divide into 8 pieces, shape tight balls and stamp each with a Kaiser roll stamp, or fold five overlapping flaps by hand. Set them stamp side down on a floured cloth for 15 minutes, then turn them over onto a lined sheet and let them rise 20 to 30 minutes more.

Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) with a tray at the bottom. Spray the rolls with water, slide them in, pour a cup of water or ice cubes into the hot tray for steam and bake 18 to 22 minutes until deep golden.
Cool on a rack so the crust stays crisp.

citations.source: Quick German Recipes, Oma's Traditional Brötchen

recipes.curationNote: Dough follows the two Brötchen recipes (Type 550 flour, yeast, water, salt, a little sugar and butter, steam baking); Wikipedia gives the star cut, the Austrian origin and the minimum weight. Fresh yeast is used in place of instant, as a German baker would. Eight rolls of about 95 g so other recipes can count rolls.

recipes.name: Rotkohl (Apfelrotkohl)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, glossy red cabbage, sweet and sour at once, with apple, clove and bay running through it.
recipes.healthBenefit: Red cabbage brings fibre, vitamin C and the purple anthocyanin pigments, and the long braise keeps it gentle to eat.
instructions: Toss the shredded cabbage with the vinegar, sugar and salt in a bowl. If there is time, leave it covered overnight in the fridge so it keeps its colour.
Melt the butter in a wide pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 4 to 5 minutes without browning.
Add the apple, then the cabbage with its liquid, the water, bay leaf, cloves and cinnamon stick. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise over low heat for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it catches, until the cabbage is soft.
Remove the bay leaf and whole spices. If it is too liquid, stir the flour into 2 tbsp water, stir it in and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until glossy.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the red cabbage and apple.

citations.source: My Dinner, German Red Cabbage with Apple
Quick German Recipes, Red Cabbage Recipes

recipes.curationNote: My Dinner, German Red Cabbage with Apple for every amount and step; serves 4 as given; ours makes 6 from the same quantities.

recipes.name: Spargel mit Sauce Hollandaise
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender, mild white asparagus under a warm, buttery, lemony sauce, with new potatoes and slices of cured ham.
recipes.healthBenefit: Asparagus brings folate and fibre and the ham adds protein; the butter sauce makes this a rich spring plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: white, peeled, woody ends cut off
200 g melted and cleared for the sauce, 5 g for the water

ingredients.prepNote: juice of half a lemon, for the sauce

instructions: Peel each spear from just below the tip downward and cut off the woody ends.

Bring a wide pot of water to the boil with 1 tsp salt, the sugar, 5 g butter and 1 tsp lemon juice. Lay in the asparagus and simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes, depending on thickness, until a knife slides in.
Meanwhile melt the 200 g butter and skim off the foam. Keep it warm, about 140°F (60°C).
Whisk the yolks with the wine in a metal bowl over barely simmering water until thick and pale, 3 to 5 minutes. Do not let the bowl get hotter than the hand can bear.
Off the heat, whisk in the warm butter in a thin stream until the sauce is thick and glossy. Season with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch each of salt and white pepper.
Lift out the asparagus, drain and plate it with the potatoes and ham. Spoon the sauce over just before serving.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the ham and egg yolks.
From the butter and yolks in the sauce.

citations.source: My Dinner, German Asparagus with Hollandaise Sauce

recipes.curationNote: My Dinner, German Asparagus with Hollandaise Sauce for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours; ham amount not given, ours kept.

recipes.name: Rahmspinat
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, finely chopped spinach in a light cream sauce with a whisper of garlic and nutmeg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Spinach brings folate, vitamin K and vitamin A, and the cream and milk carry some calcium.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: freshly grated; the source gives no amount, a usual amount
the source says to taste; a usual amount

instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling salted water for 1 to 2 minutes, drain, rinse cold and squeeze out the water, keeping a few spoonfuls of the cooking liquid.
Chop the spinach very finely by knife or pulse it briefly in a processor.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and soften the onion and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk and cream and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until it thickens, loosening with the spinach water if needed.
Stir in the spinach, season with nutmeg, salt and pepper and heat through for 2 to 3 minutes.

citations.source: Quick German Recipes, Creamed Spinach Recipe

recipes.curationNote: My Dinner, German Creamed Spinach for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours; 500 g frozen spinach, about 900 g fresh.

recipes.name: Kohlrabi in Rahmsoße
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, tender kohlrabi sticks in a mild cream sauce, flecked green with its chopped leaves and a little nutmeg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Kohlrabi is high in vitamin C and fibre and low in calories; the cream keeps the portion modest but rich.

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 bulbs, peeled and cut in sticks

ingredients.prepNote: stirred into a little cold water

instructions: Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the kohlrabi sticks, season with salt, pepper and nutmeg, pour in the vegetable stock, cover and stew for 8 to 10 minutes.
Pour in the cream and simmer uncovered 4 to 5 minutes until the kohlrabi is tender.
Stir in the starch slurry and simmer 1 minute until the sauce coats a spoon. Fold in the chopped leaves and taste for seasoning.
recipes.curationNote: Lecker, Kohlrabigemüse kochen for every amount and step; 1 onion, 2 kohlrabi of about 300 g, 1 tbsp butter, 100 ml stock, 100 ml cream, 1 tsp starch, 4 tender leaves; salt, pepper and nutmeg to taste, so our usual amounts stand.

recipes.name: Gurkensalat
recipes.flavorProfile: Cool, thin cucumber slices in a sweet-sour vinegar dressing with plenty of dill.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, hydrating salad that brings a little vitamin K and potassium with very few calories.
instructions: Toss the cucumber slices with the salt and leave them 30 to 60 minutes, then squeeze out the water they release.
Whisk the vinegar, water, sugar, pepper and oil, and stir in the onion.
Fold in the cucumbers and dill and leave 10 to 15 minutes before serving.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the cucumber skin and dill.

citations.source: Quick German Recipes, German Cucumber Salad

recipes.curationNote: My Dinner, Gurkensalat for every amount and step; serves 4: 2 cucumbers, 50 g onion, 3 tbsp vinegar, 4 tbsp oil, 2 tsp sugar, 2 tbsp dill, about 2 tsp salt for draining, pepper to taste; Quick German Recipes thins the vinegar with water.

recipes.name: Krautsalat
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, finely shaved white cabbage kneaded soft with vinegar and salt, sharpened with onion and caraway.
recipes.healthBenefit: Raw white cabbage brings vitamin C, vitamin K and fibre, with only a little oil in the dressing.
instructions: Shave the cabbage very finely and put it in a large bowl with the salt and sugar.
Knead it firmly with clean hands for about 5 minutes until it softens and releases liquid.
Add the vinegar, onion, caraway, pepper and oil and mix well.
Cover and leave at least 30 minutes, better 2 to 3 hours, then taste and season again.
recipes.curationNote: Lecker, Klassischer Krautsalat for every amount and step; 600 g cabbage, 4 tbsp white wine vinegar, 1 small onion, 1.5 tbsp oil, 1 tsp caraway; salt, sugar and pepper to taste, so our usual amounts stand.

recipes.name: Bohnensalat
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender green beans in a sharp vinegar and oil dressing with onion and the peppery note of summer savory.
recipes.healthBenefit: Green beans bring fibre, vitamin K and folate, in a dressing of sunflower oil and wine vinegar.

ingredients.prepNote: or a fresh sprig of Bohnenkraut cooked with the beans
part for the cooking water; the source says to taste

instructions: Cook the beans in salted water with the savory for 8 to 12 minutes until tender but still green. Drain, keeping 2 tbsp of the water.
Whisk the vinegar, the bean water, sugar, salt, pepper and oil, and stir in the onion.
Pour the dressing over the warm beans so they take it up, and leave 30 minutes to 1 hour before serving.
recipes.curationNote: Küchengötter, Grüner Bohnensalat for every amount and step; for 4: 500 g beans, 3 to 4 sprigs savory, 1 to 2 red onions, 4 tbsp wine vinegar, 6 tbsp sunflower oil, 3 pinches sugar, salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.name: Rahmwirsing
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft ribbons of savoy cabbage in cream, sweet and mild, with nutmeg at the back.
recipes.healthBenefit: Savoy cabbage brings vitamin C, vitamin K and fibre; the cream makes it a rich side.

instructions: Take off the outer leaves, quarter the cabbage, cut out the core and slice it into thin strips.
Melt the Butterschmalz in a large pot over medium heat and soften the onion 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the cabbage and cook about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it starts to wilt.
Pour in the cream, bring it to a gentle boil, then cover and simmer about 10 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper and serve hot.

recipes.healthBenefit: Beetroot brings folate, fibre and dietary nitrate, and walnuts add plant omega-3 fat.

recipes.name: Obatzda
recipes.flavorProfile: A soft, tangy spread of ripe Camembert mashed with butter, onion, paprika and a splash of wheat beer.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich cheese spread that brings protein and calcium; it is high in saturated fat, so a small serving with radishes and bread is the usual way.
instructions: Mash the Camembert with a fork, then work in the soft butter and cream cheese until mostly smooth with small pieces left.
Stir in the onion, paprika, cayenne, caraway, salt, pepper and beer.
Chill for 30 minutes to 1 hour so the flavours settle.
Mound it on a plate, dust with a little more paprika, scatter with chives and serve with pretzels, rye bread and radishes.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the Camembert and cream cheese.

recipes.curationNote: Both recipes mash ripe Camembert with cream cheese, butter, onion, paprika and wheat beer; butter set between them at 50 g. Wheat beer is not in the food database.

recipes.name: Zwiebelkuchen
recipes.flavorProfile: A thin yeast base under a deep layer of soft, sweet onions set in sour cream and egg, with smoky bacon and caraway.
recipes.healthBenefit: Onions bring fibre and the eggs and bacon protein; with bacon and sour cream it is a rich autumn bake.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.cutPrep: 5 g for the dough, the rest for the filling
ingredients.prepNote: 6 g (1 tsp) for the dough, 3 g for the filling, which the source leaves to taste

instructions: Stir the yeast and sugar into the lukewarm milk and leave 5 to 10 minutes. Add the flour, 6 g salt and 2 tbsp oil and knead 5 to 8 minutes to a smooth dough. Cover and let it rise 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Fry the bacon in a large pan with 1 tbsp oil until the fat runs, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the onions and cook gently, stirring, for 15 to 20 minutes until soft and pale gold. Let it cool.
Beat the sour cream with the eggs, caraway, the rest of the salt and the pepper, and stir in the onions.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough thin onto a lined baking sheet, pressing up a small rim, and spread the onion mixture over it.
Bake 35 to 45 minutes until the top is set and golden in places. Serve warm, traditionally with new wine (Federweißer).

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs, bacon and sour cream.

recipes.curationNote: My Dinner, Zwiebelkuchen (German Onion Cake) for every amount and step; 12 slices, same as ours; filling salt and pepper to taste, ours keeps usual amounts.

recipes.name: Rosenkohl mit Speck
recipes.flavorProfile: Brussels sprouts blanched until tender, then tossed in a hot pan with crisp bacon, onion and butter.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brussels sprouts are high in vitamin C, vitamin K and fibre; the bacon adds flavour, protein and salt.

ingredients.cutPrep: trimmed, a cross cut in large stems

ingredients.prepNote: a pinch; the source says to taste
mostly for the cooking water; the source says to taste
a pinch; the source says to taste

instructions: Cook the sprouts in salted boiling water for 6 to 8 minutes until just tender. Drain well.
Fry the bacon in a wide pan over medium heat for 4 to 6 minutes until crisp. Add the onion and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the butter and the sprouts and toss over medium-high heat for 3 to 5 minutes until they take a little colour.
Season with nutmeg and pepper, and a little salt if needed, and serve.

recipes.name: Laugenbrezel
recipes.flavorProfile: A deep mahogany, glossy crust with coarse salt, a crisp split belly and thin, crunchy arms around a soft, chewy middle.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly wheat carbohydrate with a little protein; the pretzel salt makes it a salty bread, so it sits best beside fresh food.

components.note: the whole batch, with its lye bath and salt

instructions: Make the Laugenteig and divide it into 8 pieces. Roll each into a rope 50 to 60 cm long, thick in the middle and thin at the ends.
Lift the ends, cross them twice and press them onto the thick belly. Lay the pretzels on a floured cloth and chill them uncovered for 1 hour so a skin forms.
Dip each pretzel in the lye bath for 10 to 15 seconds, wearing gloves, and set it on a tray lined with baking paper. Sprinkle with coarse salt and cut the belly once, about 5 mm deep.
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 15 to 20 minutes until deep brown. Cool on a rack and eat the same day, plain or split and buttered as a Butterbrezel.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the dough salt and the coarse pretzel salt.

citations.source: Quick German Recipes, German Pretzel Recipe

recipes.curationNote: The dough, lye bath and salt sit in the Laugenteig base; this recipe is the shaping and baking. Both recipe sources dip in lye (or baking soda) and cut the belly; Wikipedia gives the Swabian shape with thin arms and a fat belly.

recipes.name: Laugenbrötchen
recipes.flavorProfile: A round roll with the dark, salty pretzel crust and a soft, close crumb, split for butter, cheese or Leberkäse.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly wheat carbohydrate with a little protein, and salty from the crust; good split and filled with vegetables and cheese.

components.note: the whole batch, shaped as rolls

instructions: Make the Laugenteig and divide it into 8 pieces of about 105 g. Shape each into a tight ball by rolling it under a cupped hand on the bench.
Set the rolls on a floured cloth seam side down and chill them uncovered for 1 hour so a skin forms.
Dip each roll in the lye bath for 10 to 15 seconds, wearing gloves, and set it on a tray lined with baking paper. Cut a cross or a single slash on top and sprinkle with coarse salt.
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 16 to 20 minutes until deep brown. Cool on a rack.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the dough salt and the coarse salt on top.

recipes.name: Roggenmischbrot
recipes.flavorProfile: A dark-crusted loaf, mostly rye, with a moist, close crumb and a mild sourness.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rye flour brings more fibre than white wheat, and the sourdough makes its minerals easier to take up.

ingredients.cutPrep: lukewarm, about 350 ml for the pre-dough and 3 to 4 tbsp for the yeast

instructions: The evening before, mix 250 g of the rye flour, all the wheat flour, the sourdough starter and about 350 ml lukewarm water to a dough. Cover and leave overnight at room temperature.
Next day, dissolve the yeast in 3 to 4 tbsp lukewarm water, work it into the pre-dough and leave it 30 minutes.
Knead in the rest of the rye flour, the salt and the sugar. Cover and let it rest about 3 hours.
Shape a round loaf on a floured bench, set it on a lined baking sheet and let it rise 1 more hour.
Heat the oven to 480°F (250°C). Put the loaf in, turn the oven straight down to 355°F (180°C) and bake 60 to 75 minutes.
Switch the oven off and leave the loaf inside 10 minutes more, then cool on a rack.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the rye and Type 1050 wheat flour.

recipes.name: Vollkornbrot
recipes.flavorProfile: A dense, moist, dark tin loaf of whole rye with linseed and sunflower seeds, gently sour and nutty.
recipes.healthBenefit: Whole rye and seeds bring a lot of fibre, magnesium and plant omega-3 fat, which makes the bread filling.

ingredients.cutPrep: half worked in, half on top
shelled, half worked in, half on top
about 150 ml lukewarm for the pre-dough, 350 ml for the dough

instructions: Have everything at room temperature. Mix both flours in a large bowl and make a well in the middle. Crumble in the yeast, sprinkle the sugar over it and pour in about 150 ml lukewarm water. Stir in a little flour from the edge to a thick batter, cover and leave 15 minutes until it bubbles.

Add the remaining 350 ml water, the sourdough starter, the bread spice and the salt and mix everything. Knead on a floured bench 5 to 10 minutes until smooth, return it to the bowl, cover and let it rise in a warm place about 1.5 hours, until doubled.

Knead briefly and work in half the sunflower seeds and linseed. Shape a loaf, dust it with flour and set it in a greased loaf tin. Scatter the rest of the seeds on top and let it rise about 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 445°F (230°C). Brush the loaf with water and prick it a few times with a fork. Bake 15 minutes, then lower to 390°F (200°C) and bake about 1 hour more. Cool completely before slicing.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the whole rye, wholemeal wheat and seeds.
From the whole rye and sunflower seeds.

recipes.name: Bauernbrot
recipes.flavorProfile: A round, floury farmhouse loaf with a thick, cracked crust and a soft, mildly sour crumb of rye and wheat.
recipes.healthBenefit: The rye half brings more fibre and minerals than a white loaf, and the sourdough makes them easier to take up.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and maple syrup in the lukewarm water. Add both flours, the sourdough starter and the salt and knead to a smooth dough.
Cover and let it rise about 1.5 hours, until clearly bigger.
Knead again briefly, shape two loaves (or one large one) and set them on a lined baking sheet. Cover and let them rise 1 hour.

Heat the oven to 480°F (250°C). Bake the loaves a few minutes, then lower to 390°F (200°C) and bake about 30 minutes more, until they sound hollow underneath. A single large loaf needs longer. Cool on a rack.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the darker flours and the yeast.

recipes.name: Dinkelbrot
recipes.flavorProfile: A light, nutty spelt loaf with a crisp crust, a soft crumb and toasted sunflower seeds.
recipes.healthBenefit: Wholemeal spelt brings fibre, magnesium and B vitamins; spelt is a wheat and contains gluten.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 130 g in the dough, the rest for the top

instructions: Butter a 30 cm loaf tin.
Crumble the yeast into the lukewarm water and stir until dissolved. Stir in the salt and the cider vinegar.
Mix in the spelt flour and most of the sunflower seeds to a soft, sticky dough; it needs no kneading.
Spread the dough in the tin, scatter the rest of the seeds over the top and let it rise 20 minutes.
Bake in a 390°F (200°C) fan oven for about 1 hour. Turn it out and cool on a rack.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the wholemeal spelt and sunflower seeds.
From the wholemeal spelt and seeds.

recipes.name: Hefezopf
recipes.flavorProfile: A soft, golden, slightly sweet braided loaf scented with lemon, studded with raisins and topped with almonds.
recipes.healthBenefit: A sweet bread made with butter, egg and milk; a treat for Sunday breakfast rather than an everyday loaf.

ingredients.cutPrep: soaked in warm water 15 minutes and dried

instructions: Make the Hefeteig and, after its first rise, knead in the raisins.
Divide the dough into 3 equal pieces and roll each into a rope about 40 cm long. Press the tops together and braid them loosely, tucking the ends under.
Set the braid on a lined baking sheet, cover and let it rise 30 to 40 minutes.
Brush with the yolk beaten with the water and scatter with the almonds.
Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden, covering loosely with foil if it browns too fast. Cool on a rack.

recipes.name: Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte (Black Forest Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: Light chocolate sponge soaked with cherry brandy, layered with tart cherries and cool whipped cream, finished with chocolate shavings.
recipes.healthBenefit: A celebration cake rich in cream and sugar; the sour cherries bring some vitamin C and the cocoa some minerals, but it is a treat.

ingredients.prepNote: split between the cherries and the cream

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line the base of a 26 cm springform tin.
Beat the egg whites with the hot water until stiff, then beat in the sugar until glossy and stir in the yolks.
Sift the flour, cornstarch, cocoa and baking powder over the eggs and fold in gently.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean, and leave to cool fully, ideally overnight.

Bring most of the cherry juice to a boil, whisk the cornstarch and sugar into the rest, stir it in and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until thick. Fold in the cherries and half the vanilla and leave to cool.
Cut the sponge into three layers and drizzle each with Kirschwasser.
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar and the rest of the vanilla until stiff.
Spread the cherries over the bottom layer, cover with cream, add the second layer and more cream, then the top layer.
Cover the whole cake with cream, pipe rosettes on top, scatter with chocolate shavings and chill for 2 to 3 hours before slicing.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the whipping cream and egg yolks.
A little from the cocoa and dark chocolate.

citations.source: Quick German Recipes, Black Forest Cake Recipe

recipes.curationNote: Both sources build a cocoa sponge without butter, cut it into three layers, soak with Kirschwasser and fill with thickened sour cherries and cream. Quantities follow My Dinner. Kirschwasser and powdered sugar are not in the food database.

recipes.name: Apfelstrudel
recipes.flavorProfile: Paper-thin, crisp pastry wrapped around soft cinnamon apples, raisins and buttery toasted crumbs, served warm.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly apple by weight, so it brings fibre and some vitamin C, with butter and sugar making it a dessert.

ingredients.prepNote: for dusting; 2 tbsp at 7.8 g per tbsp

instructions: Knead the flour, water, oil and a pinch of salt for 8 to 10 minutes into a smooth, soft dough, brush with a little oil and rest it covered for 30 to 60 minutes.
Soak the raisins in the rum. Toss the apples with the lemon juice, sugar, vanilla sugar, a pinch of cinnamon, the raisins and the almonds.
Toast the breadcrumbs in 40 g of the butter until golden, then set aside.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll the dough out on a large floured cloth, then stretch it over the backs of your hands until it is thin enough to read through, and trim the thick edges.
Brush the dough with melted butter, scatter the crumbs over two thirds of it and spread the apples over the crumbs.
Lift the cloth to roll the strudel up, tuck in the ends and roll it seam side down onto a lined tray.
Brush with butter and bake for 35 to 45 minutes, brushing again halfway, until golden and crisp.
Rest for 10 minutes, dust with powdered sugar and serve warm, with vanilla sauce or whipped cream.

recipes.name: Bienenstich (Bee Sting Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft sweet yeast cake under a crackly honey and almond crust, split and filled with cool vanilla cream.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich coffee-table cake; the almonds bring vitamin E and the milk some calcium alongside plenty of sugar and butter.

components.note: half the batch, about 250 g flour

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Press half the risen Hefeteig into a lined 26 cm springform tin and leave it to rise for 20 to 30 minutes.
Melt the butter, sugar and honey together, stir in the almonds and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until slightly thickened, then cool for a few minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Spread the almond mixture over the dough and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden; cool completely.
Whisk a little of the milk with the yolks, cornstarch and sugar. Bring the rest of the milk to a boil, whisk in the yolk mixture and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until thick.
Take the pudding off the heat, stir in the vanilla and the squeezed gelatine until dissolved, and cool until just setting.
Fold the whipped cream into the cooled pudding.
Cut the cake in half horizontally, cut the almond top into 12 wedges, spread the cream on the base and lay the wedges back on top.
Chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the milk and cream in the filling.

recipes.name: Käsekuchen (German Quark Cheesecake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A tall, light, gently tangy quark filling scented with lemon and vanilla on a crisp shortcrust base.
recipes.healthBenefit: Quark makes this cheesecake higher in protein and lighter than cream cheese versions, though it is still a sweet dessert.

components.note: the whole batch, lining the tin

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Roll out the Mürbeteig and line a greased 26 to 28 cm springform tin, bringing it 4 cm up the sides; chill while you make the filling.
Beat the quark, sugar, cream, eggs, cornstarch, vanilla and lemon zest together until smooth.
Pour the filling into the tin and smooth the top.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until set at the edges and just wobbly in the middle; cover with foil if it browns too fast.
Turn off the oven and leave the cake inside with the door slightly open for 20 to 30 minutes so it does not crack, then cool completely and chill before slicing.

recipes.name: Streuselkuchen (Crumb Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft sweet yeast cake under a thick layer of buttery vanilla crumbs, moistened with a little cream.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain coffee cake of flour, butter and sugar; small squares make it an occasional treat.

components.note: the whole batch, for one baking tray

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tsp for the streusel, 1 tsp for the cream

instructions: Roll the risen Hefeteig out onto a lined baking tray (about 30 × 40 cm), cover and leave to rise for 20 to 30 minutes.
Rub the cold butter, flour, sugar and vanilla together with your fingertips into large and small crumbs; chill them.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Press shallow dimples into the dough with your fingers and brush it with the melted butter.
Scatter the streusel thickly over the dough and sprinkle with the sugar.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the crumbs are golden.
Stir the rest of the vanilla into the cream, drizzle it over the hot cake so it soaks in, cool, dust with powdered sugar and cut into 24 squares.

recipes.name: Zwetschgendatschi (Bavarian Plum Sheet Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin yeast dough packed edge to edge with tart, jammy plums under cinnamon crumbs, best with a spoon of whipped cream.

Stand the plum halves upright and close together in rows over the whole dough, cut side up.
Rub the flour, sugar, butter, cinnamon and vanilla into crumbs and scatter them over the plums.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25 to 35 minutes, until the dough is golden underneath and the plums are soft.
Cool on the tray, cut into 20 pieces and serve with whipped cream.

recipes.name: Frankfurter Kranz (Frankfurt Crown Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A ring of light sponge layered with vanilla buttercream and raspberry jam, coated in crunchy caramelised almond brittle.
recipes.healthBenefit: One of the richest German cakes, high in butter and sugar; the almonds add vitamin E, and a thin slice goes a long way.

components.note: 190 g, red currant jam is also traditional

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter and flour a 26 cm ring (Kranz) tin.
Beat the eggs and sugar for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and pale, then fold in the sifted flour, cornstarch and baking powder.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, turn out and leave to cool completely.

Whisk a little milk with the cornstarch, sugar, yolk and vanilla; boil the rest of the milk, whisk the mixture in and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until thick. Cover the surface and cool to room temperature.
Beat the butter with the powdered sugar for 5 minutes until fluffy, then beat in the cooled pudding a spoonful at a time.
For the Krokant, melt the sugar with the butter to a golden caramel, stir in the almonds, spread on baking paper to cool, then crush finely.
Cut the ring into three layers; spread the bottom two with jam and buttercream and stack them.
Coat the whole ring with buttercream, press the Krokant all over, pipe a few rosettes on top and set the raspberries on them. Chill for 2 hours before slicing.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the almonds in the brittle.
From the butter and egg yolks.

recipes.name: Donauwelle (Danube Wave Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: Marbled vanilla and chocolate sheet cake with sour cherries sunk into it, a thick layer of vanilla buttercream and a wavy chocolate top.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich sheet cake heavy in butter and sugar; the cherries and dark chocolate bring a little fibre and iron.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Make the pudding first: whisk a little milk with the yolks, cornstarch, sugar and vanilla, boil the rest of the milk, whisk the mixture in and cook for 1 to 2 minutes. Cover the surface and cool to room temperature.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and line a deep baking tray (about 30 × 40 cm).
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the flour and baking powder.
Spread half the batter on the tray. Stir the cocoa and a splash of milk into the rest and spread it over the light layer.
Scatter the cherries over the top and press them in lightly; bake for 25 to 30 minutes and cool completely.
Beat the soft butter until pale, then beat in the room-temperature pudding a spoonful at a time and spread it over the cake. Chill for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate with the oil, spread it over the buttercream and draw waves through it with a fork or a cake comb before it sets.
Chill until firm and cut into 24 pieces with a hot knife.

recipes.name: Kaiserschmarrn (Torn Emperor's Pancake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, fluffy pancake torn into pieces and caramelised in butter, studded with raisins and served with apple sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs and milk give it protein, and the apple sauce adds fruit; the butter and sugar make it a hearty sweet meal rather than a light one.

Heat the oil and half the butter in a large ovenproof pan, pour in the batter and scatter the drained raisins over it.
Cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until set underneath, then bake for 8 to 10 minutes until puffed and golden.

recipes.name: Germknödel (Plum-Filled Yeast Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: A big, pillowy steamed yeast dumpling with dark spiced plum butter inside, drenched in melted butter, poppy seed sugar and vanilla sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Poppy seeds bring calcium and the plum butter some fibre, but with butter and vanilla sauce this is a filling, rich sweet dish.

ingredients.prepNote: 2 tsp for the dough, 1 tsp for the sauce
stirred into the plum butter, optional
mixed with the poppy seed; 2 tbsp at 7.8 g per tbsp

instructions: Stir the yeast and a pinch of the sugar into the lukewarm milk and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.

Knead it with the flour, remaining sugar, soft butter, yolks, salt, 2 tsp of the vanilla and the lemon zest for 5 to 8 minutes into a smooth dough; cover and leave to rise for 45 to 60 minutes until doubled.
Stir the rum into the Pflaumenmus. Divide the dough into 4, flatten each, put 1 tbsp of plum butter in the middle, pinch the dough closed and roll into a ball.
Leave the dumplings to rise, seam side down, for 15 to 20 minutes.
Steam them over simmering water, or in a covered pan over a cloth stretched above boiling water, for 15 to 20 minutes without lifting the lid.

Meanwhile make the vanilla sauce: whisk the yolks with the cornstarch, whisk in the milk heated with the sugar, and stir over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes until it coats a spoon; add the rest of the vanilla.
Serve each dumpling in a deep plate with melted butter poured over, a thick layer of poppy seed and powdered sugar, and the vanilla sauce around it.

From the butter and egg yolks.

recipes.name: Dampfnudeln (Steamed Yeast Buns)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, fluffy yeast buns steamed in sweet milk and butter until a caramelised, crackling crust forms underneath, with vanilla sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Milk and eggs bring protein and calcium; it is a sweet, filling dish traditionally eaten as a meal in itself.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Stir the yeast and a pinch of the sugar into the lukewarm water and leave for 10 minutes until bubbly.
Cream the butter with the rest of the dough sugar, mix in the eggs, milk, salt and yeast, then enough flour for a soft dough; knead until smooth.
Cover and leave to rise for about 1 hour until doubled, then shape into 8 balls and leave to rise for 30 minutes more.
In a wide pan with a tight lid, heat the steaming milk, butter, sugar, a pinch of salt, half the vanilla and the lemon zest.
Set the buns in the pan, cover and cook over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes without lifting the lid, until the milk has gone and you hear a crackle as the bottoms caramelise.

While they cook, make the vanilla sauce: whisk the yolks with the cornstarch, whisk in the milk heated with the sugar, stir over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes until it coats a spoon, and add the rest of the vanilla.
Lift the buns out crust side up and serve warm with the vanilla sauce.

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and lay the Oblaten on lined baking trays.

Fold in the ground almonds and hazelnuts, the chopped candied peel, the baking powder and the spice into a soft, sticky mass.

Glaze half with melted chocolate and half with the powdered sugar icing while still warm, then cool and store in a tin for a few days to soften further.

recipes.name: Christstollen (Christmas Stollen)
recipes.flavorProfile: A dense, buttery yeast loaf full of rum-soaked raisins, almonds and candied peel around a seam of marzipan, under a thick coat of sugar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rich in butter and dried fruit, a Christmas bread eaten in thin slices; the almonds and raisins add some fibre and minerals.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Soak the raisins in the warm water and rum for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight, then drain.
Stir the yeast into the lukewarm milk with 100 g of the flour and leave this starter for 45 minutes.
Toast the flaked almonds on a tray at 400°F (200°C) for 8 to 10 minutes until golden, then cool. Lower the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Knead the starter with the remaining flour, sugar, salt, spice, vanilla and soft butter into a firm dough, then knead in the raisins, almonds and candied peel just until spread through.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 to 2 hours; the dough rises only a little.
Flatten the dough into an oval, lay the marzipan log along the middle, fold one long side over so it does not quite meet the other and press the edge to make the stollen shape.
Bake on a lined tray for 50 to 60 minutes, covering with foil if it browns too fast.
Brush the hot stollen all over with melted butter, roll it in the sugar, cool, then cover thickly with powdered sugar.
Wrap well and leave for 1 to 3 weeks before slicing, so the flavors settle.

recipes.name: Berliner Pfannkuchen (Jam Doughnuts)
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, golden fried yeast doughnuts with a pale ring around the middle, filled with tart jam and rolled in sugar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fried and sweet, made for carnival and New Year's Eve; a treat rather than a source of much nutrition.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: about what is taken up from 750 ml for frying

instructions: Stir the yeast and sugar into the lukewarm milk and leave for 10 minutes until it bubbles.
Add the flour, butter, vanilla and salt, pour in the yeast milk and knead, adding the yolks one at a time, for 5 to 8 minutes into a smooth, elastic dough.
Cover and leave to rise for about 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces of about 60 g, roll each into a tight ball, set on a floured cloth, cover and leave to rise for 30 to 40 minutes.
Heat the oil to 340°F (170°C). Fry 3 or 4 at a time, covered for the first 2 minutes, then turn and fry uncovered for 2 to 3 minutes more, until golden with a pale ring around the middle.
Drain on paper, then pipe the jam into each through a small hole in the side.
Roll in or dust with sugar and eat the same day.

recipes.name: Marmorkuchen (Marble Cake)

recipes.healthBenefit: A classic butter cake for coffee time; eggs bring some protein and cocoa a little iron, alongside plenty of sugar and butter.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter a 22 cm Gugelhupf or Bundt tin and dust it with flour.
Beat the butter, sugar and vanilla for 3 to 4 minutes until light, then beat in the eggs one at a time and mix in the cream.
Sift in the flour, baking powder and salt and fold just until combined.
Spoon two thirds of the batter into the tin. Stir the cocoa into the rest and spread it on top.
Draw a fork through both batters in a spiral to marble them.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 10 minutes in the tin, then turn out.
Melt the chocolate with the butter and pour it over the cooled cake.

recipes.name: Apfelpfannkuchen (Apple Pancakes)

instructions: Whisk the egg whites with a pinch of the salt until stiff.

Fold in the egg whites and rest the batter in the fridge for about 30 minutes.
Toss the apple wedges with the lemon juice and brown sugar.

recipes.name: Bratapfel (Baked Apple with Vanilla Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, sweet-sour whole apples filled with caramelised nuts, raisins, cinnamon and marzipan, in a pool of warm vanilla sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: A whole apple each brings fibre and some vitamin C, and the nuts add vitamin E; the vanilla sauce and marzipan make it a winter dessert.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: about 1 tbsp; or the seeds of 1 vanilla pod, as the method describes

instructions: Soak the raisins in the rum, ideally the night before. Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Toast the nuts in a dry pan, stirring, for 3 to 5 minutes until they smell roasted, then add the butter and brown sugar and stir until caramelised.
Off the heat, stir in the raisins, cinnamon and lemon juice, then knead in the marzipan to a paste.
Fill the cored apples with the nut mixture and stand them in a buttered baking dish.
Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until the apples are soft but still hold their shape.

For the vanilla sauce, whisk a little milk with the cornstarch, sugar, salt and yolks. Heat the rest of the milk with the vanilla pod and seeds, whisk in the mixture and stir over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes until thick, then remove the pod.
Serve the hot apples in the warm vanilla sauce.

recipes.name: Spekulatius (Spiced Shortcrust Biscuits)

Bake on lined trays for 10 to 12 minutes, until golden brown at the edges.
Cool on a rack and store in a tin.
